messages:
elaine: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking out loud about swapping to a lease-first admission model for fairness. pros/cons?
aj: can you sketch the high-level flow you mean? leases vs current token-bucket paths are tripping me up.
elaine: flow: ingress -> local short-lived lease (ms) -> central broker for longer leases when load high -> fallback queue. Local leases keep latency low, central leases give global fairness.
mike: sounds fine but main risk is freshness and double-counting when a request migrates between nodes. we need idempotent lease attach/detach semantics.
sara: +1 on idempotency. also need clear signals for abuse prevention. if we give long leases we might amplify noisy clients. how do we revoke quickly?
jin: revoke path should be through a soft-grace flag. mark lease "revoked" and let in-flight finish, deny new attaches. that avoids mid-token cancellations.
elaine: yeah, revoke + soft-drain. still debating open questions: 1) lease granularity (per-tenant vs per-route), 2) accounting (tokens vs request-units), 3) interface (sync gRPC vs async pubsub).
aj: for 1, per-route is friendlier for PLG customers who want per-model budgets. per-tenant is simpler to reason about for fairness across apps. maybe hierarchical: tenant -> route.
mike: hierarchical makes sense but increases bookkeeping. for 2 we should try request-units where possible (tokens depend on model variant). RU lets us normalize.
sara: agree on RU. for 3 I prefer gRPC for fast attach/detach, but pubsub is better for eventual topology changes and evictions. hybrid? grpc for requests, pubsub for control-plane events.
jin: hybrid + lease TTLs solves many cases. short TTL local leases (~100ms) via grpc; longer central leases via broker + pubsub invalidations.
elaine: flagging abuse: if score > threshold, deny central leases and drop to strict token-bucket local only. this keeps latency but limits throughput.
aj: what about graceful degradation? clients should see 429 or degraded model fallback. we should define a standard header: X-Redwood-Degrade: <reason>.
mike: also add metrics: lease_acquire_latency, lease_revocations, lease_bounces, abuse_deny_count. need SLIs for false-positives (good clients flagged).
sara: operational playbook: 1) detect surge -> escalate to probation window -> restrict central leases -> monitor error increase -> roll back. keep human-in-loop for first month.
jin: API surface: AcquireLease(tenant_id, route, requested_ru, hint_timeout_ms) returns lease_id, granted_ru, ttl_ms, policy_flags. ReleaseLease(lease_id) async. InvalidateLease(lease_id) published to pubsub.
elaine: love the AcquireLease sketch. aj can you write a tiny proto stub next week?
aj: yep, will stub and post in rfc channel. quick Q: do we persist leases for auditing?
mike: persist only metadata (lease_id, tenant, granted_ru, ttl, revoke_flag) to async store for a few days. heavy persistence hurts path.
sara: note: eviction must notify billing to prevent surprises. link billing event: lease_evicted -> billing.alert if > X RU lost.
elaine: ops-bot can we add a cron check to surface large revocations to #oncall?
ops-bot: scheduled check created: daily lease-revocations summary -> #eng-oncall at 09:00 UTC.
elaine: ok next steps: aj proto, mike telemetry plan, jin control-plane pubsub sketch, sara ops playbook. keep thread short updates here. :thumbsup:
